newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says seeks damages for Belgian beef ban.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says seeks damages for Belgian beef ban.

text.p: Egypt intends to seek compensation and maintain its ban on beef imported from Belgium until authorities provide information on penalties imposed on two firms because of the mad cow crisis, an official said.

An Egyptian order in July banned imports of beef from Belgium after the European Commission said 1,600 tonnes of British beef was exported, with Belgian help, to Egypt, Russia, and Netherlands despite a ban imposed because of mad cow.

"The Ministry of Supply and Trade announces that the decision to ban the import of beef from Belgium, published on July 3, is still in effect," said Ibrahim al-Baz in the letter to the editor published in Al-Akhbar newspaper.
Baz is the head of central administration for the office affairs of Minister of Supply and Trade Ahmed Gueily.

"This ban will not be lifted except in the case of official notification by the Belgian government and European Union authorities of punishment imposed on the two companies, involved in falsifying the certificates of origin of the meat and with which the ministry banned dealing, so that the ministry is able to take necessary steps to file a case against them for damages," the letter said.
Baz did not name the companies and had no further comment when contacted by Reuters.
"Mad cow" disease is the more commonly used term to describe the brain-wasting Creutzfeld-Jakob Disease which scientists have linked to bovine spongiform encephalopathy.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said in remarks published in July that authorities took steps to ensure that Egypt was free of beef infected with mad cow disease.
His statement in Al-Gomhuria newspaper said Egyptian authorities had discovered an attempt to ship British beef into Egypt using Belgian documents.
